nodes.label: Mi Recetario
nodes.rationale: Web app for organizing recipes; ingestion is delegated to an automated n8n flow rather than an app-owned backend.

nodes.label: Supabase database (direct JS client)
nodes.rationale: README specifies the JS client is used directly ('cliente JS directo') — no server-side data access layer is described between the SPA and the database.

nodes.label: n8n webhook recipe ingestion
nodes.rationale: Automation (ingestion, deletion, email sharing) is pushed to n8n webhooks so the static SPA never needs its own server process. The app derives the three routes /nueva-receta, /eliminar-receta and /compartir-receta from a single configured base URL.

nodes.label: Catalogo module (masonry recipe viewer)
nodes.rationale: Masonry layout plus an ingredient-based search is chosen as the read surface over recipes stored in Supabase.

nodes.label: Anadir Receta module (PDF upload form)
nodes.rationale: Kept deliberately simple: the form only ships a recipe PDF to the n8n flow, so all parsing and persistence logic lives outside the frontend.

nodes.label: Environment configuration (.env variables)
nodes.rationale: VITE_SUPABASE_URL, VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and VITE_N8N_WEBHOOK_BASE are externalized to .env (copied from .env.example) so deployment targets differ only by configuration, not code.

nodes.label: npm run build (production bundle)
nodes.rationale: Produces a /dist folder whose contents are copied to the Nginx web root; the build is the entire deployment artifact.

nodes.label: Nginx SPA fallback configuration
nodes.rationale: try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html is required because client-side routing means non-root URLs have no corresponding file on disk.

nodes.label: Static SPA deployment on home Nginx server
nodes.rationale: The app is designed as a purely static SPA so it can be served from a domestic Nginx instance with no application runtime, which is what forces both data access and automation out to external services.
nodes.norm_label: static spa deployment on home nginx server

nodes.label: Supabase JS client with no backend layer
nodes.rationale: The read path (Stack -> Supabase JS client -> Supabase project gtqqqmethhakpybnuxin) deliberately bypasses an app-owned server; this is the same architectural answer as the n8n write path, applied to the opposite direction of the same database.
nodes.norm_label: supabase js client with no backend layer

nodes.label: Secrets policy: no hardcoded credentials
nodes.rationale: Policy is honored for Supabase (credentials read from VITE_SUPABASE_URL / VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY at src/lib/supabase.ts:3-4) and violated for n8n, whose three endpoint URLs are hardcoded string literals.

nodes.label: Hardcoded n8n webhook URLs (secrets-policy violation)
nodes.rationale: Code verification found all three n8n endpoints written as literals in source rather than derived from VITE_N8N_WEBHOOK_BASE as the README claims.

nodes.label: eliminar-receta webhook (undocumented, useRecipes.ts:108)
nodes.rationale: Present in code but absent from README, which documents only the ingestion webhook — the graph undercounted n8n's surface as a result.

nodes.label: compartir-receta webhook (undocumented, useRecipes.ts:129)
nodes.rationale: Present in code but absent from README; handles email sharing of a recipe.

nodes.label: n8n as de-facto backend layer
nodes.rationale: The 'no backend layer' claim in AGENTS.md is contradicted in practice: n8n owns write, delete and share operations against the same Supabase database, making it a server tier by another name.
